title: Fluid Push-to-Talk
description: A native macOS voice app for fast dictation, local commands, daily-note capture, and hands-free Hermes Agent control.
body:
Fluid Push-to-Talk is a native macOS voice app for turning short spoken input into useful computer output. It is built for the way I work: hold a hotkey, speak, release, and the result lands where it should go.

The simple mode is fast dictation. Hold Command + Option, talk, and the app transcribes the audio locally with FluidAudio and pastes the text into the active field. That is useful for messages, notes, prompts, and any place where typing would slow me down.

## What it does

- Records voice through clear push-to-talk shortcuts.
- Runs local speech recognition on the Mac instead of sending every word through a web app.
- Pastes plain dictation into the current app.
- Turns a second gesture into a local command flow, so the transcript can become a rewritten text, a structured answer, or a short action result.
- Opens or reuses a real Hermes Agent terminal session for agent work.
- Sends voice instructions to Hermes in the foreground, then brings the answer back to the place where the user started.
- Supports Obsidian daily-note capture and a continuous dump mode for longer spoken notes.
- Keeps Bluetooth keyboard output optional and off by default, so setup is safer for normal users.

## Recent work

The June work turned the app from a personal prototype into something closer to a customer installer. The installer can clone or update the public fork, build the Swift app, link the command, reset state when asked, and guide the user through setup. The setup flow now keeps API keys in an environment file instead of JSON config, and it supports OpenAI-compatible providers instead of only one local path.

The hotkey system also became cleaner. Bluetooth keyboard mode is disabled by default, audio input routing is configurable, and the app can work better with headsets and external devices. The Hermes mode was hardened so a voice instruction opens the correct foreground terminal session and submits the exact prompt visibly. That matters because agent work should be inspectable, not hidden in a background process.

## Value for users

The value is speed and less friction. A user can speak, paste, rewrite, dump notes, or hand work to an agent without switching through many apps. The app is local-first where it should be local, but it still connects to hosted LLMs or Hermes when that is the better tool.

## Current direction

The current direction is reliability. The app should start cleanly, explain setup clearly, recover from missing keys or permissions, and keep the microphone, terminal session, and clipboard behavior predictable. For a voice tool, small mistakes feel big. The next versions should keep reducing surprise while making the core flow faster.

## Public boundary

The public page describes the app behavior and installer shape. It does not publish private config values, API keys, local prompts, or personal daily-note content.
